hints.title: Use the given turning point
hints.body: A quadratic with vertex (h,k) has form a(x−h)2+k. Insert the turning point (−1,3).
hints.recap: Completed-square form records the vertex directly.
hints.pitfall: A curve passing through the point need not have its turning point there.
hints.pause: Write <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with only a left unknown.

recall.reminder: Completed-square form records the vertex directly.

hints.title: Use the other point
hints.body: The vertex form is a(x+1)2+3. Since (1,−1) lies on the graph, −1=4a+3.
hints.recap: A second point determines the scale of a quadratic with known vertex.
hints.pitfall: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, the squared bracket is 4, not 2.

recall.reminder: A second point determines the scale of a quadratic with known vertex.

hints.title: Expand and check
hints.body: Substitute a into a(x+1)2+3 and expand into the form used by the options.
hints.recap: Expand only after the geometric information has fixed the parameters.
hints.pitfall: Remember both the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> term and the constant from the square.
hints.pause: Check the final expression at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and at its vertex.

recall.reminder: Expand only after the geometric information has fixed the parameters.

solution:
A quadratic with turning point (−1,3) must have form f(x)=a(x+1)2+3, with a≠0. Passing through (1,−1) gives −1=a(2)2+3, so a=−1.

Hence f(x)=−(x+1)2+3=−x2−2x+2, option A. This expression gives f(1)=−1 and has its maximum at (−1,3), so it meets both conditions.
knowledgePattern: Recover a quadratic from its vertex and one point
